Overview: what is going on, in one page
Every Univest blog should have a big heading of 60 letters or fewer. This page shows how many blogs are too long, how many we have already fixed, and how many are still waiting.

  
All the blogs on the site, and where each one stands
Every blog that was too long at the start is placed in one of two matched halves (twins, not luck). TEST blogs get the short heading. NOT TESTED blogs stay as they are, so we can compare the two halves.
Every blog, with its link

    

    

  
READ THIS FIRST
Start is for YESTERDAY's blogs (and any older blogs not changed yet). Blogs posted today are only recorded in tab 3. Tomorrow morning, when you open this tab and press Start, today's blogs get their new headings and show up in tab 2 (Yesterday) with link and proof.

    

      

        
The fix

        

        
Start changes every one of today's TEST headings that is ready. For each blog it changes the heading (Fix 1), changes the SEO title only if it is over 60 letters (Fix 2), refreshes the site copy with the revalidate link, saves a proof screenshot and checks the live page. The NOT TESTED half and any blog you left out are never touched. Nothing changes until you press Start.

        

      

      

    

  


  
The analysis, with every source
Everything the tool says is backed by one of the studies below. Each has what I did, the numbers, and links so anyone can open the pages and check.


  
Replacement research: how every new heading is chosen
This is the rule. Every replacement heading, for every blog, goes through the same steps, every time. The daily tool follows them in code, and anyone rewriting a "check first" heading follows the same checklist.


  
Test: old long headings vs new short headings
Does a short heading really change the traffic? We find out with a fair test: half of the blogs keep the long heading, half get the short one, and we watch both every day.


  
Today: the 50/50 fix
Every blog written or edited today that has a heading over 60 letters is split into two exact halves. TEST gets the new researched heading. NOT TESTED keeps its long heading, so we can see if the change makes any difference. Nothing changes until a person presses Start.








Start (a person reviews, then presses)




  
Done today: changed live, validated, with proof
Every blog changed today, with the two fixes (the big heading and the SEO title), the proof screenshot of the revalidate link, and the live check. Tap a screenshot to enlarge it.


  
Explain the test: why, how, and what "same" means
The test only means something if the two halves are alike. So we do not split by chance or by count. We make twins.

  
Tracker: is the change working?
Is the 50/50 split making a difference? For every blog we changed: its numbers before, its numbers after, and how the blogs we did not touch are doing at the same time. Numbers come from Search Console and arrive about 3 days late.

How it works

      
Scan
Reads the blog lists (about 77,600 blogs). New and changed blogs first, then the oldest-checked.

      
Count
Counts the letters in each big heading. More than 60 is a flaw.

      
Write
Drafts a short heading: drops "Ltd", company codes and repeated names.

      
Start
One press, and every ready heading is replaced in WordPress. The blog link stays the same.

    
Fixes are drafted by rules. "Check" ones should be read by a person first. Headings that would become the same as another blog's are skipped.
Public blog pages can take a while to show a new heading, because the site keeps a saved copy of each page.
The crawl of all blogs is still going, so the numbers grow until every blog is checked.
